system.summary: 6x6 digit square, each letter a vertical pair of digits 1-6 (top over bottom), with some thirty graphic signs for words or names.
system.notes: Same 6x6 vertical-digit-pair square as R1892; word signs partly fixed from page-1 clear text.

prior_solution.where: page 1 carries its own clear Dutch under the cipher; pages 3-4 not deciphered anywhere

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched R2242 record and four images with the session cookie.
DECODE note points to R1892; same vertical digit pairs, so tried the R1892 key.
One ciphered word in the clear page 2: 24 43 25 55 15 15 65 = famille.
Two subagents transcribed p1 (4 lines), p3 (17 lines), p4 (8 lines + P.S.).
Page 1 clear Dutch under the cipher agrees with the R1892-key decrypt and fixes ~12 word signs.
p3-p4 decrypted with the R1892 key: alliance, scattered troops, Basel ratification, ambassadors to Paris, Robespierrism.

Word signs in p3-p4 read from context and re-checked on the photographs: script L = uit, flagged D-shape = van, phi = Frankrijk (I); perp = om (M, also fits R1892 p2); the ratification passage and the Robespierismus sentence now read without gaps except the sign '&'. Dating consequence: the treaty 'with France' puts p3-p4 after 16 May 1795.
DECODE images not in the checkout; a cookie download returned a 5 kB placeholder; the 21 Sept rotated full-resolution copies were recovered from the old worktree .worktrees/r2242 and copied to img/.
p3 l1 re-transcribed at full resolution: every pair confirmed ('braaden wat zeid men [van] onse alliansie met').

p4 l8 re-transcribed: 32->22 ('woort'), final 42->52 ('broer', a 4 overwritten by 5); 13 32 11 'ynt' is as written, read 'antwoort' as the writer's 1-for-4 slip (M). Also p4 l6 43->34 ('is het'), p1 l4 11->55 ('dienst'), p3 l2 margin 'offeciers', five doubtful pairs given their probable values.

Word signs from context, pooled with R1892: Lambda = dat (M, three R1892 contexts agree), slashed/crossed Lambda = dat, infinity = daar (M, 'daar ... van voorstellen'), < = naar, check-over-bar = zonder (M), crossed e = zijn (M), X = weinig, crossed x = al, & = Engeland, + = mogelyk, crossed diamond = voor, Y-crossbar = ik, crossed Y = dez-.

Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken I-II full text (resources.huygens.knaw.nl retroboeken) searched for Grasveld, Sitter, Blaauw, Robespierismus, gebraaden, persisteeren, saamenhang, gedimitteerde, verstrooid, Banquier, rassemblement, ratificatie; GS II pp. 834-841 read. The letter is not printed.

The interlinear insertion 'sitteren [inverted D] grasveld' = '[de] Sitter en [van] Grasveld', the extraordinary envoys to Paris (GS I p. 655), and 'Meier en Blaauw' = the negotiators Blauw and Meyer (GS I no. 507): fixes the inverted D = van and dates p3-p4 to late May-June 1795.

Remaining single signs tried and not adopted: plain Delta (Staaten / zyde each fit one context), T-bar and S-stroke ('goeds', 'kan'), psi and H-loop on p4 l8, %, C-hook, crossed o, V-with-cross, H-with-P, dagger, square/vertical brackets, x mark, Delta-with-tail, P.S. signs.

Measured with apply.py --measure and measure_sense.py (nl-modern, 13-char window > -4.3, calibrated on p1 and letter-shuffled controls): tokens given a value 95.2% -> 97.9% (1,015/1,037); tokens read as sense 86.0% -> 94.6% (981/1,037).

Sense measure made strict and fairer (measure_sense.py): STRICT=1 counts I-grade sign values as unread; a token also passes inside an attested 6+-letter word (lang/ nl corpus + Gedenkstukken I-II OCR, fetch_gedenkstukken.py); y scored as ij for Dutch. Letter-shuffled control passes 8.4% (max 12.2%), unchanged by the word check.

Grades re-examined under a forced-context rule (M = several contexts agree or grammar admits one word): script L uit, phi Frankrijk, crossed Y dez-, slashed/crossed Lambda dat, Y-crossbar ik, crossed x al, < naar upgraded to M; X weinig, & Engeland, + mogelyk, crossed diamond voor stay I and count unread.
Every token failing the sense test checked on the image: p3 l6 31->34 (saamenhang); p4 l3 'persisteern' confirmed as the writer's (t e e r n).

Read as sense, strict: 941/1,037 = 90.7% (HEAD transcription, 30 Sept signs) -> 940 (2 Oct, LM only) -> 953 (+word check) -> 979 (+forced upgrades) -> 994/1,037 = 95.9% (+y as ij). With I values: 1,000/1,037 = 96.4%.
Gaps re-sorted: signs occurring twice (Delta, %, crossed diamond) stay open-codes; the nineteen true singletons are blocked by no-key-material (one context cannot fix a word sign).

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The 6x6 digit-square key the project had recovered ciphertext-only for R1892 (KHA Prins Willem V inv. 339) read this letter (KHA Koning Willem I XVIII-3) unchanged, as DECODE's own note on R2242 suggested; the clear Dutch written under page 1 confirmed it and fixed about a dozen word signs.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription_p1/p3/p4.txt with STRICT=1 apply.py --measure (3 Oct 2026): 1,010 of 1,037 cipher tokens given an H or M value (I-grade sign values counted unread; 1,015 with them). p1 111/111.
outcome.notes: All digit pairs map with the R1892 key. Read as sense (STRICT=1 measure_sense.py, nl-modern, LM window or attested word, y as ij): 994/1,037 = 95.9% (p1 100%, p3 95.7%, p4 94.5%); 90.7% for the 30 Sept state under the same measure. Meets the read bar; classed read on 3 Oct 2026 (the letter as a whole; p3 95.7%, p4 94.5% on their own). Twenty single word signs and four I-grade signs open; letter not in Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken I-II.
